The Zuni tribe have perplexed anthropologists with their language. They speak a language that is too similar to Japanese to be coincidental. Anthropologists can't figure out why this would be the case.

Some similar words as an example. Clan in Zuni is 'kwe,' in Japanese 'kwai.' The word for priest is 'shawani' in Japanese and 'shiwani' in Zuni. Both Zuni and Japanese use the verb as the last word of a sentence, a feature only 45% of languages share. This might not seem like much, but the Zuni language is very different in this than other languages around them.

This sparked some research and scientist discovered that both Zuni and the Japanese have similar frequency of Type B blood, a rare kind of kidney disease and very specific oral traditions about their origins. The working theory is that Buddhist missionaries somehow made it to California around the 12th century somehow.
There's a tribe in New Mexico that speaks a language eerily similar to Japanese

[criticism]

While this is still unexplained, the working theory is that there is a "mother language" of Asian languages. Why the Zuni only have it, I'm not sure. It's presumed there were more than 1 mass exodus from eurasia, and if this is so, the latter would have to be on boats. Boats, resembling the asian design have been found as low as the gulf, but preservation does not led well in the salty waters of the Pacific.

It is possible that they crossed by boat later than 15000 YBP, when the japanese language was being formed. It could explain it. Without archaeological evidence, however, this is merely speculation.

I use unique bur only with 110 and 125 jacketed. For a point of reference, how much unique would you typically use for your light loads?

I haven't ever used unique, trail boss has been working well for me. I just loaded up some test rounds with 700x and will test them tomorrow. I'll let you guys know how it goes

Edit: Work ran long today. I am going to have to keep everybody in suspense for 1 more day.
I'm using 5.5 gr. with 115 plated FP's for a good plinking / small game load. Fun to shoot all afternoon, easy on the brass, and leaves the barrel fairly clean.

Well I got to test my 700x loads today and it went great. I loaded 2.5 grains up to 3.9 grains in .2 increments behind a 125 grain truncated cone. 3.5 grains and up shot very clean, below that was just a little bit dirty. I have decided to go with the lowest I tried at 2.5 , they were just so light and easy to use and they were clean enough.

I've had good results with 3.3 gr Red Dot w/Berry's hard cast 158 SWC. This load works well in a 7.5" Ruger Bisley as well as an 18" 77/357. No felt recoil in the carbine, and virtually none in the revolver. They're reasonably clean and feed well from the rotary magazine.
